image_description: A medium shot of a three-person band performing on an elevated stage. From left to right: a guitarist with long hair playing a sunburst electric guitar, a bassist in the center playing a white bass, and a lead singer on the right holding a microphone. The background features a large banner with partial text/logos. Stage monitors (wedge speakers) are visible at the bottom edge.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elevated rectangular platform, raised slightly above floor level.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The subjects are clearly standing on a raised surface relative to the implied audience level, confirmed by the presence of wedge monitors at their feet which sit on the stage floor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dimensions vary from small intimate platforms to large theatrical stages spanning the full width of a performance hall.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is cropped tightly on the performers; the full width and total dimensions of the stage structure are not visible.
The line where the stage floor meets the vertical drop (obscured by monitors) is visually distinct, defining the boundary of the performance area.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface is covered with matte black flooring or painted wood.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The floor beneath the musicians' feet appears to be a dark, non-reflective material consistent with standard stage decking.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Steps or ramps provide access from floor level.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Access points (stairs/ramps) are typically located at the sides or rear of a stage and are outside the current camera frame.
The top of the image cuts off at the backdrop banner height; overhead trusses and lighting fixtures are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Constructed from wood or metal decking.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the substructure is hidden, the surface texture and rigidity implied by the standing figures support the presence of standard decking materials.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface shows scuff marks from performances.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The resolution and lighting conditions make it impossible to definitively identify specific scuff marks or wear patterns on the dark floor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Side and rear may have wings or backdrop supports.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large printed backdrop/banner is clearly visible behind the performers, serving as the rear visual boundary of the stage setup.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The text/logos on the backdrop are partially illegible and morphologically inconsistent, typical of AI generation struggling with complex typography, though less severe than complete gibberish.
Slight softness and indistinct finger definition on the fretting hand; the connection between fingers and strings lacks crisp physical contact clarity.
The white bass guitar has a slightly warped body shape and the strap connection point appears ambiguous/fused with the clothing.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'text_gibberish' artifact. In real photos, out-of-focus text blurs but retains character structure. In AI images, characters often melt into each other. Verify if the background text is merely blurry or structurally nonsensical. Also, scrutinize the bassist's white guitar for warping, as white objects on dark backgrounds often reveal edge-detection failures in AI models.
